points.description: States that a higher priority process is not getting the CPU (is kept waiting/blocked) because of a lower priority process. Equivalent wording such as 'high-priority task is blocked by low-priority task' earns the mark.

Gives the reason: the lower priority process holds a resource (lock, semaphore, mutex or similar) that the higher priority process needs. Equivalent wording such as 'low-priority task holds the shared resource' earns the mark.
